title: Valerse de: utilizar algo en beneficio propio

sections.content: Valerse de (to make use of, to avail oneself of) describes using a tool, opportunity, or resource to one's own advantage -- often carrying a hint that the thing used was seized skillfully, or even opportunistically. It's followed by a noun phrase. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El acuerdo se valió de una reforma constitucional para permitir la reelección presidencial inmediata.
items.english: The agreement made use of a constitutional reform to allow immediate presidential reelection.

items.spanish: Menem se valió directamente de esta reforma de 1994 para presentarse a la reelección en 1995.
items.english: Menem directly made use of this 1994 reform to run for reelection in 1995.

items.spanish: Menem se valió también de un estilo personal muy particular para consolidar su popularidad.
items.english: Menem also made use of a very particular personal style to build his popularity.

items.spanish: Otros líderes de la región se valdrían, en los años siguientes, de estrategias políticas similares.
items.english: Other leaders in the region would make use of, in the following years, similar political strategies.

sections.content: Valerse de is reflexive and always takes de before its object -- don't drop the de, and remember the subject is the one doing the using, not the thing being used.
